recognize_zh: 低倍圓形視野中有數個大型、立體重疊的細胞團，細胞核大、核質比高、排列擁擠並互相擠壓，與左側單個良性間皮細胞及散在的小淋巴球大小差異明顯，符合肺癌轉移至肋膜積液。
features: Several cohesive three-dimensional clusters of large cells with crowded, overlapping nuclei
High N:C ratio with enlarged round to oval hyperchromatic nuclei and nuclear molding
Basophilic cytoplasm with frayed, finely vacuolated edges on some groups
Isolated benign mesothelial cell with central nucleus and pale cytoplasm for size comparison (left)
Scattered lymphocytes and occasional red cells in a clean background
describe_en: Pleural fluid cytospin at low to intermediate power shows several cohesive, three-dimensional clusters of large atypical cells with crowded, overlapping hyperchromatic nuclei and high nuclear-to-cytoplasmic ratios. These groups contrast with a single benign-appearing mesothelial cell and scattered small lymphocytes in the background. Nuclear detail is limited at this magnification. Findings are consistent with metastatic carcinoma involving the pleural fluid in a patient with known lung cancer, with cell block immunocytochemistry recommended for confirmation.

ddx.vs: Reactive mesothelial groups are flat or papillary with intercellular windows, low N:C ratio and uniform nuclei, and are calretinin/WT1 positive and Ber-EP4/MOC-31 negative.
Mesothelioma can form cell balls but is calretinin, WT1 and D2-40 positive with BAP1 loss, whereas lung adenocarcinoma is TTF-1 and MOC-31 positive.
Small cell carcinoma shows smaller cells with scant cytoplasm, finely granular chromatin, prominent molding in chains and absent nucleoli.
